note: Every organisation, place, person, figure and sentence in this file is invented. Hosts use the reserved .example top-level domain. Nothing here is, or is derived from, a real source.

cases.title: An announcement whose text states no date
cases.rationale: The release date is when it was PUBLISHED. The text gives no date for any project event, so `event_date` must stay empty (ADR 0004: missing dates remain missing).

documents.title: An announcement whose text states no date
documents.text: Brindlemoor Foods will build a new 280,000 square foot manufacturing plant in Carrow Ridge, Tennessee, a $210 million investment that will create 240 jobs.

cases.title: A forecast start is an interval, not an event date
cases.rationale: A stated expectation ("is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027") belongs in the temporal interval fields, never in `event_date`, and never as the publication date.

documents.title: A forecast start is an interval, not an event date
documents.text: Brindlemoor Foods will build a new 280,000 square foot manufacturing plant in Carrow Ridge, Tennessee, a $210 million investment that will create 240 jobs. Construction is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027.

cases.title: A stated past event, published eight days later
cases.rationale: The text states the groundbreaking happened on May 12; the release is dated May 20. When the text states the date, that date (not the publication date) is the event date.

documents.title: A stated past event, published eight days later
documents.text: On May 12, 2026, Tessaly Bottling Company held a groundbreaking ceremony for its new $180 million bottling plant in Ashgrove Mill, Wisconsin, creating 150 jobs.

cases.title: CONTROL: a source that states no publication date
cases.rationale: With no publication date the pipeline writes no event date. This is the one behaviour of the date path that is already correct, and it must survive the repair.
